snippet.title: BC wildfire that’s been deemed out-of-control forces multiple evacuations
snippet.description:
Residents of North Bend, B.C. are being ordered to evacuate as an out of control wildfire continues to grow in the Fraser Canyon.
 
The fire, just outside the community of Boston Bar, has reached 100 hectares in size, the B.C. Wildfire Service said in an alert issued early Sunday morning.
 
The fire has been steadily growing since it was first discovered on Thursday. Officials say they believe the fire was caused by human activity. An evacuation alert has also been put in place for the entire community of Boston Bar.
 
Residents are being advised to gather family members, pets, and essential items such as government ID, and be ready to leave at a moment’s notice.
 
Global's Angela Jung reports.

For more info, please go to https://globalnews.ca/news/11953588/wildfire-evacuation-fraser-valley-bc/

snippet.title: How to Survive a Grid Failure That Doesn’t End
snippet.description:
Keep your family safe and steady when the grid goes down — even if you live in town. Join our *free live class* this Thursday: https://www.thereadylife.com/GridDownHome

A former US congressman who helped create our nation's EMP commission sat down with us to explain a threat most people never see coming...electromagnetic pulse. It's a single event, solar or man-made, that could take down the power grid for months or even years. What he told us about replacement transformers, the 1989 Quebec collapse, and the three-day food supply in our cities will change how you think about being ready.

The bigger lesson goes deeper than shielding your electronics. Even if you have your own off-grid solar or a generator, your life still gets turned upside down when everyone else loses power — trucks stop running and store shelves empty in about three days. The real goal is getting your family to where you don't depend on the grid for your next drink of water, your next meal, or warmth in the winter. We break down what an EMP really is, why the grid won't simply bounce back, and the simple, low-cost steps to build redundancy into your water, heat, food, and power.

- What an EMP is, the three pulses (E1, E2, E3), and how a solar storm differs from a nuclear blast
- Why replacement transformers could leave the grid down for months — and what Carrington and Quebec already proved
- The low-cost way to protect spare electronics, plus the first water redundancy step worth taking now

*Find Your Weakest Link Before the Grid Does*
This Thursday, Nick and Lisa are hosting a free live class — How to Make Your Home Grid-Down Ready, Even If You're in Town. You'll walk through the four systems that actually keep your family safe when the power's gone, and you'll leave with one clear next step for your home. It's free, it's live, and your seat is waiting: https://www.thereadylife.com/GridDownHome

*Build a Backup Power Plan That Actually Works*
If protecting your power is on your list, the *Emergency Power Toolkit* helps you size the right generator, portable power station, and backup setup for your real needs — so you can keep your fridge, your well, and your essentials running when the grid goes down. snippet.title: The Most Realistic Grid-Down Scenario You Need To Prep For
snippet.description:
Is a long-term grid-down event actually on the horizon? We hear warnings all the time about cyberattacks, EMPs, solar flares, failing infrastructure, and even coordinated attacks potentially taking down the U.S. power grid for months or longer.

But how realistic is that?

After more than 15 years of preparedness, I've heard plenty of predictions about the next disaster that was supposedly right around the corner. In this video, I talk about a recent conversation I had with my son about the possibility of a large-scale grid failure and why I look at these threats differently today.

A complete nationwide grid-down event may be a low-probability, extremely high-impact scenario. Regional and extended power outages, however, are much more realistic—and preparing for those situations can also put you in a much better position if something bigger ever happens.

I talk about potential threats to the power grid, including cyberattacks, physical attacks on infrastructure, EMPs, CMEs and aging grid infrastructure, along with why I focus my preparedness on the events most likely to actually affect my family.

Are you concerned about a long-term power grid failure? And how long are you prepared to live without the grid?

snippet.title: Evacuation orders expand for Big Sur as Timber Fire grows to 800 acres
snippet.description:
The Timber Fire has grown to 800 acres in Monterey County and remains 5% contained Monday morning as evacuation orders and warnings remain in effect for areas of Big Sur.

CAL FIRE reported the fire at 800 acres and 5% containment in an incident update issued at 6:26 a.m. Monday. The fire had been reported at 400 acres and 5% containment Sunday night.

The Monterey County Sheriff’s Office issued an immediate evacuation order at 11 p.m. Sunday for zones MRY-F026, MRY-F027 and a part of MRY-F028. The evacuation order includes the Ventana Inn

“LEAVE NOW!” the sheriff’s office said in announcing the orders.

An evacuation order means people should leave the affected area because of an immediate threat to life and property. Officials are urging residents in evacuation order zones to take their families, pets, and emergency supply kits, and to consider bringing essential documents and records.

snippet.title: Period prep 🌸 #antiinflammatory
snippet.description:
Girl, it's almost that time of the month 🤍 Our bodies are basically in inflammation warfare during our period, so this week I'm fueling mine with foods that fight back. Here's everything I prepped…

🍲 Chicken and Lentil Soup
Recipe: Chicken, red lentils, spinach, carrots, celery, bell peppers, onion, garlic, cumin, turmeric, black pepper, and Kettle Fire chicken bone broth.

Why this soup: it's iron, magnesium, and anti-inflammatory goodness in one pot. The lentils and spinach replace the iron you're losing so you're not dragging, the magnesium helps with the cramps, and the vitamin C in the peppers helps your body actually absorb that iron. Carrots, celery, and the bone broth help with bloating, turmeric and garlic calm the inflammation, and the warmth alone is soothing when you're cramping.

🐟 Salmon and Veggie Medley
Omega-3s from the salmon to calm cramp inflammation, iron and magnesium from the kale.

🌺 Hibiscus Cinnamon Cooler
Antioxidants to fight inflammation, cinnamon for the cramps.

🍍 Pineapple Turmeric Popsicles
Pineapple and turmeric are BOTH inflammation warriors. For when that sweet tooth hits. (But also, please have a sweet dessert too girl!)

🧖‍♀️ And self care is part of the prep too. On my face: the Kiehls Rare Earth Clay Face Mask for Pores and Uneven Texture

This is what works for my body, not medical advice. Listen to yours 🤎

Hope this helps for your next period prep. #periods #womenshealth #antiinflammatory


Update! Recipe below:

**Chicken and Lentil Soup**

Ingredients:
- Chicken breasts, seasoned however you like
- 2 cups red lentils (dry)
- 3 to 4 celery stalks, diced
- 4 carrots, diced
- 1 bell pepper, diced
- 1 onion, diced
- 1.5 cartons Kettle Fire chicken bone broth
- 1 bag spinach

Seasoning: turmeric, cumin, and chicken bouillon, italian seasoning, to taste 

Method:
1. Cook the chicken first, then shred it  and set aside.
2. In the same pot, cook the onion, carrots, celery, and bell pepper with the seasoning until softened.
3. Add the bone broth, then the shredded chicken back in.
4. After about 15 minutes, rinse the lentils and add them in. Simmer.
5. Lastly, stir in the whole bag of spinach.

snippet.title: These 8 Items Are USELESS After an EMP — Stop Stockpiling Them
snippet.description:
#PrepperPantry #Stockpile #FoodShortage2026
Your bug-out bag has a $200 paperweight in it right now. You just don't know it yet — because it still turns on today.
An EMP doesn't care what you paid. It doesn't care about the brand. It doesn't care about the military-grade label on the packaging or the five-star reviews or the prepper influencer who told you it was the one piece of gear you couldn't skip. It cares about one thing — whether the device contains a semiconductor junction longer than a specific threshold length. If it does, the induced voltage destroys it. Permanently. No reset. No repair. No warranty claim. Eight items that dominate prepper gear lists, bug-out bags, and Amazon survival storefronts worldwide contain exactly that vulnerability — and the community has collectively spent millions of dollars stockpiling them as if an EMP doesn't exist.
Here's the part that makes this genuinely dangerous rather than just expensive. Most of these eight items don't have a manual backup. They were designed in an era that assumes electricity is permanent. The engineers who built them never considered a scenario where the grid doesn't just go down but stays down — because that scenario doesn't exist in commercial product development. snippet.title: Los MILLONARIOS se preparan para SOBREVIVIR a algo que podría cambiarlo TODO | De Todo Un Mucho
snippet.description:
😳 ¿Por qué algunos de los hombres más ricos y poderosos del mundo están invirtiendo millones en búnkers, propiedades autosuficientes y refugios capaces de funcionar durante una emergencia?

En este episodio de De Todo Un Mucho, Martha Higareda y Yordi Rosado hablan sobre el creciente interés por prepararse para escenarios extremos y sobre los millonarios que han construido o invertido en enormes propiedades con infraestructura subterránea.

Uno de los casos que analizamos es el de Mark Zuckerberg y su enorme propiedad en Hawái, donde se ha reportado la existencia de infraestructura subterránea, puertas reforzadas, sistemas de agua, producción de alimentos y otras medidas de autosuficiencia.

Pero Zuckerberg no es el único caso.

También hablamos de los llamados “preppers”, de refugios privados, propiedades aisladas y hasta complejos subterráneos diseñados para albergar comunidades completas en caso de una emergencia.

🏢 Y aquí es donde la realidad empieza a recordar demasiado a SILO.

Existen complejos de supervivencia con filtración para amenazas nucleares, biológicas y químicas, cultivo hidropónico, áreas médicas, gimnasio, alberca, espacios para mascotas y sistemas pensados para que una comunidad pueda permanecer bajo tierra.

Entonces surge la gran pregunta del episodio:

¿Por qué algunas de las personas con mayor acceso a dinero, tecnología e información están gastando fortunas en estar preparadas?

¿Se trata simplemente de multimillonarios tomando precauciones ante guerras, pandemias, desastres naturales o posibles crisis… o perciben riesgos que la mayoría de nosotros todavía no estamos tomando en serio?

👀 Y después de ver todo esto, la comparación con SILO resulta inevitable: ¿podríamos llegar algún día al punto de construir sociedades enteras debajo de la tierra?

👇 Cuéntanos en los comentarios: si tuvieras los recursos necesarios, ¿construirías tu propio búnker?
